relatedSnapshot.title: Master: Add Leads submits the AI Search text as the campaign niche, so a search over the 120-character label cap fails the scrape with a raw validation error
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

The Add Leads lead scraper and the campaign write path disagree about how long a campaign niche may be. The scraper's AI Search box accepts up to 200 characters and submits that text as the campaign's niche label, while the create/update schema rejects any niche over 120. A search falling in that gap blocks lead scraping outright and shows the user a serialized validation array instead of a field message.

## Problem

In Cold Email Agent, an operator adding leads to an existing campaign types a description into the AI Search box, clicks through to Add Leads, confirms, and gets `Failed to start lead scraping: [{"code":"too_big","maximum":120,...,"message":"Niche must be 120 characters or less","path":["niche"]}]`. Nothing is dispatched, no lead scrape run is created, and the message does not read like something the operator can act on in the form. The same defect was reported in July 2026 by a different organization and was closed by asking the customer to shorten the niche, so the cause has been left in place.

## Root cause

Two maximums apply to one string on the Add Leads path.

* `apps/web/components/campaigns/new/steps/ai-search-inline-view.tsx` renders the AI Search input with `maxLength={MAX_NICHE_SEARCH_PROMPT_LENGTH}`, which is 200 (`apps/web/lib/outreach/campaign-niche-intent.ts`).
* `apps/web/components/campaigns/new/steps/lead-scraper-filters.tsx`: `handleSearch()` copies the box text into `submittedNiche`, and `buildFormData()` returns it as `niche`; `handleConfirmLeads()` passes that to `onNext`.
* `apps/web/components/campaigns/campaign-scrape-leads-client.tsx` `handleScrapeLeads()` sends it to `outreach.campaigns.createOrUpdateCampaign`, and its `onError` renders `Failed to start lead scraping: ${error.message}`.
* `apps/web/lib/outreach/schemas/campaigns.ts` `createCampaignInputSchema` caps `niche` at `MAX_CAMPAIGN_NICHE_LABEL_LENGTH` = 120. The comment there records the intent that UI paths cap the input and the server guard only covers API and direct-tRPC callers, and `campaign-niche-intent.ts` line 110 states the cap is "Enforced at every niche input". The Add Leads path honours neither.
* The same submitted string is accepted up to 200 by `outreach.providers.inferFromNiche` (`apps/web/trpc/routers/outreach/providers.ts`), so one flow validates the identical value at two different maximums.

This descends from the work that made a niche a short label and set the acceptance criterion that every niche input enforces the 120-character cap; the add-leads entry point was left uncapped.

Not the cause: the approval-targeting seed (`buildApprovalFormData`) is only used in approval mode, which submits `saveApprovalLeadSearchTargeting` with its own 120 cap and a different toast, and the ordinary campaign seed passes through `sanitizeTransientNiche`, which blanks anything over 120. An approval-seeded or stored niche cannot produce the observed toast.

## Blast radius

Confirmed affected, counted 2026-09-24: 2 organizations two months apart, 1 user in each, from two independent customer reports (the July 2026 report and the September 2026 one).

Potentially exposed: not countable from production. A rejection in input validation writes no row and leaves no run, so the blocked-organization count needs error instrumentation or support-side reports.

Legacy data that is context, not exposure: 76 campaigns across 64 organizations hold a niche of 121-200 characters and 259 campaigns across 167 organizations hold any niche over 120, all created between 2025-10 and 2026-06-22, before this cap shipped on 2026-06-26. Those values are blanked on seed by `sanitizeTransientNiche`, so they cannot reproduce this failure, and they do not indicate the write guard being bypassed.

Queries: `SELECT count(*) AS n, count(DISTINCT organization_id) AS orgs FROM outreach_campaign WHERE length(niche) > 120 AND length(niche) <= 200;` and the same with `length(niche) > 120` alone, plus a `date_trunc('month', created_at)` grouping that shows the newest over-cap row is 2026-06.

## Proposed fix

Make the Add Leads path and the write schema agree on one maximum for the niche: cap the AI Search input that feeds the niche at the label limit, or stop using the AI Search prompt as the niche label at all, and answer an over-long value with a field-level message on the search box rather than the serialized validator output. The behaviour should hold for every entry point that funnels into `createOrUpdateCampaign`.

## What's included

In scope: the Add Leads scraper to `createOrUpdateCampaign` path, the AI Search input, and the field-level error. Excluded: the legacy stored over-cap niches, which a documented cleanup already treats as values the current write policy cannot produce. Related, not part of this fix: the approval save mutation caps the same field at 120 with the default validator message, which is unfriendly but not the observed failure.

## Regression seam

The boundary between the scraper's submit payload and `createCampaignInputSchema` on `niche`: a 121-200 character AI Search text must either be capped in the input or answered with a field-level message, and must never reach the operator as a serialized validation array with the scrape blocked.

## Done when

* An AI Search text between 121 and 200 characters can no longer block a scrape: it is either prevented at the input or reported as a field error.
* A failed submit leaves the operator with an actionable message rather than a serialized validator payload.
* A regression test covers the seam above with a red-before, green-after assertion.

## Reports

* ENG-14219

relatedSnapshot.title: Customer report: Add Leads scraper submits the AI Search text as the campaign niche, so a search over the 120-character label cap fails with a raw validation error
relatedSnapshot.description:
**Intercom source**: <url:app.intercom.com>

**Conversation context**: A long-running agency thread with an operator who runs several workspaces. Name 1 reports in the same thread are already handled: the campaign lead-count question was closed (ENG-13866, Done) and the "Slots Sent" thread with no slots email behind it is tracked as ENG-14110 under master ENG-14111. On 2026-09-23 the customer posted a screenshot captioned "can't scrape leads.." showing the **Add Leads To Campaign** dialog in the Cold Email Agent over a lead preview, with the toast: `Failed to start lead scraping: [ { "code": "too_big", "maximum": 120, "type": "string", "inclusive": true, "exact": false, "message": "Niche must be 120 characters or less", "path": [ "niche" ] } ]`. The same dialog showed 9,136 estimated available leads, 10,132 lead credits remaining, and the campaign leads badge "Within Limit", so neither credits nor lead capacity was the blocker. The customer replied "still the same" on 2026-09-24 after being told to refresh.

**Claim**: In the Add Leads lead scraper, the text typed into the AI Search box is submitted as the campaign's niche label, but that box accepts 200 characters while the campaign write path caps the niche at 120, so any search between 121 and 200 characters fails the scrape and the user is shown the raw server validation dump instead of a field error.

**Evidence** (read at commit b8321a38cd373c0837eec2fe0e2bc8317d14fc69):

* The AI Search input caps input at `MAX_NICHE_SEARCH_PROMPT_LENGTH = 200` (apps/web/components/campaigns/new/steps/ai-search-inline-view.tsx, and the same 200 in ai-search-dialog.tsx).
* The scraper turns that typed text into the niche: `apps/web/components/campaigns/new/steps/lead-scraper-filters.tsx` keeps `nicheInput`/`submittedNiche` state and `buildFormData()` returns `niche: isPlaceholderNiche(submittedNiche) ? '' : submittedNiche`; `handleConfirmLeads()` passes it to `onNext`.
* `apps/web/components/campaigns/campaign-scrape-leads-client.tsx` `handleScrapeLeads()` sends that niche to `outreach.campaigns.createOrUpdateCampaign`, and its `onError` renders `Failed to start lead scraping: ${error.message}`.
* The write schema caps the niche at `MAX_CAMPAIGN_NICHE_LABEL_LENGTH = 120` (apps/web/lib/outreach/schemas/campaigns.ts, `createCampaignInputSchema`), with the stated intent that "UI paths also cap input length" and the server guard only covers API and direct-tRPC callers. The same submission reaches `outreach.providers.inferFromNiche`, which accepts up to 200 (apps/web/trpc/routers/outreach/providers.ts), so the product itself validates the identical string at two different maximums.
* A second uncapped entry point exists: `buildApprovalFormData()` in the same client seeds the scraper's search box from the campaign agent's stored targeting with `niche: targeting.niche?.trim()`, and that targeting type has no length cap (apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/campaign/types.ts, `niche: z.string()`, and `saveCampaignInputSchema`).

**Blast radius** (counted 2026-09-24 against production): 76 live campaigns across 64 organizations hold a niche between 121 and 200 characters, and 259 campaigns across 167 organizations hold any niche over the 120-character label cap, so the value class that triggers this error is already stored in production despite the write guard.

**Unverified**: the exact string the customer submitted and which entry point produced it (typed AI Search text or an agent-seeded niche) are visible only in the customer's session, so the failing value itself is not in production data.

**Excluded**: the "No email accounts connected" banner the customer also raised in the same thread is the known display-only defect ENG-10717; the campaign's sending is healthy (3,210 of 6,107 leads contacted with the newest contact event at 2026-09-23T20:56:17Z).

relatedSnapshot.title: Cold email agent: stop campaigns inheriting targeting from onboarding (certified data only) + clean existing
relatedSnapshot.description:
Parent: ENG-10462. Reworked from item **5**. PR 4 of 4. PR: Institute-of-Business-Growth/ai-clients#4868

## Overview

When someone finishes onboarding and creates their FIRST cold email campaign, the niche field (the short label for who it targets) is helpfully pre-filled with the niche they just chose in onboarding, and they can edit it. For every campaign AFTER that, the field starts empty, so a campaign never silently assumes a niche that may have drifted as the person experimented. Onboarding data is never copied into a campaign's stored targeting behind the scenes, and the autonomous agent never assumes it. This keeps the first campaign friction-free while stopping a stale niche from spreading from one campaign to the next and making campaigns look messy or wrong.

## Problem

Onboarding niche/ICP data leaked into `campaign.niche` (which should be a short 1 to 4 word label) through two seams, and there was no guard stopping an over-long value from being stored:

1. **Service-side inheritance (silent).** `OutreachService` read the onboarding selected niche (`getSelectedNicheFromSubmissions().bestOption.name`) into a `defaultNiche` and passed it into `resolveSpawnNiche` as a fallback (`apps/web/lib/outreach/services/out-reach-service.ts` around :1056, :1252, :1365). A campaign with no explicit niche therefore inherited the onboarding selection when lead search / agent runs were spawned, with no user review.
2. **Form prefill (on every campaign).** The campaign form auto-filled EVERY new campaign's niche from the onboarding selection (`apps/web/hooks/campaign/use-campaign-form.ts`, fed by a `getSelectedNiche` query). Because the onboarding niche drifts as people re-run the niche tool, campaigns created later got a stale value.
3. **No write-boundary cap.** `resolveSpawnNiche` (`apps/web/lib/outreach/campaign-niche-intent.ts`) had a `clean(campaignNiche) || clean(defaultNiche) || clean(industry)` chain and nothing capped niche length on write, so a multi-sentence brief could be persisted into `campaign.niche` and reused.

The fix is to keep the helpful prefill ONLY where the onboarding niche is genuinely fresh (the user's first campaign, editable and confirmed on save), and to stop every silent/automatic path (the agent and later campaigns) from sourcing onboarding data.

**Important real-world nuance (read-only prod evidence):** the *longest* niches are dominated by two OTHER sources, not onboarding: the AI Lead Search description persisted verbatim as the niche (`apps/web/.../lead-scraper-filters.tsx:524`) and an uncapped leads-metadata industry join. Onboarding inheritance is a real but minority contributor. Those two sources, and any input-length UI/validation, are out of scope here and handled in ENG-10579.

## Solution / What changed

1. **First-campaign-only niche prefill.** `apps/web/hooks/campaign/use-campaign-form.ts` pre-fills the create-form niche from the onboarding selection ONLY on the org's first campaign (when no campaigns exist yet), as an editable value. Every subsequent campaign starts with an empty niche, so a drifted onboarding niche is never assumed. (Previously this prefill fired on every create; it is now first-campaign-gated.) `apps/web/hooks/campaign/use-campaign-dashboard.ts` supplies the onboarding niche (`getSelectedNiche`) and a lightweight first-campaign signal (org has no existing campaigns) to gate it.
2. `apps/web/lib/outreach/campaign-niche-intent.ts` — removed the onboarding `defaultNiche` fallback from `resolveSpawnNiche`; it now resolves explicit per-campaign `campaignNiche`, then the campaign's own leads-derived `industry`, and nothing else. Added `sanitizeCampaignNiche` (write-boundary backstop that blanks a value over `MAX_CAMPAIGN_NICHE_LENGTH` = 120) and `isPlausibleShortCampaignNiche` (the trust gate for agent inheritance).
3. `apps/web/lib/outreach/services/out-reach-service.ts` — stopped reading the onboarding selected niche as `defaultNiche`; both `resolveSpawnNiche` call sites now pass only `campaignNiche` + leads-derived `industry`. The campaign's-own-leads metadata derivation (industry/title/location) is kept (certified).
4. `apps/web/lib/outreach/db/campaign.ts` — applied `sanitizeCampaignNiche` at every niche write boundary: `updateCampaign`, `createCampaign`, and `bulkUpsertCampaigns` / duplicate path.
5. `apps/web/trpc/routers/outreach/campaigns.ts` (agent start-new-campaign CSV fallback) — the replacement campaign's niche is resolved through the same trust gate as the source: an explicit empty value clears, a non-empty incoming niche is kept only if it passes `isPlausibleShortCampaignNiche` + `sanitizeCampaignNiche`, otherwise it falls back to the gated source niche. Programmatic paths sanitize-and-fall-back (no hard validation error).
6. `apps/web/scripts/cleanup-onboarding-inherited-campaign-niche.ts` (new; ops-run, dry-run by default, NOT executed by this PR) — one-time cleanup that blanks bad existing niches by two signals: (a) over the write cap (invalid stored value), and (b) an exact match to one of the org's onboarding NicheResearcher selections, temporally guarded and RESTRICTED to ops-reviewed campaign IDs (`REVIEWED_CAMPAIGN_IDS`). Niche-only; all-orgs apply requires `CONFIRM_ALL_ORGS=true`.
7. **Tests** — niche-intent (sanitizer blanks over-cap, inheritance gate), duplicate-campaign-niche (gated + sanitized duplicate path), approval-review-fixes (start-new clear/gating), plus first-campaign-prefill coverage.

## Scope

**In scope**

* First-campaign-only onboarding niche prefill (editable); subsequent campaigns start empty.
* Sever every silent/automatic onboarding niche source (agent service fallback + later-campaign form prefill).
* DB write-boundary niche backstop (blank anything over 120 chars on create/update/duplicate).
* Gate niche inheritance in the agent start-new / duplicate flows.
* One-time ops cleanup script for already-polluted niches (niche column only).

**Out of scope**

* Any NEW input-length UI or validation (no `maxLength` field, no new length error message). The existing 120-char write-boundary backstop is unchanged.
* The AI Lead Search niche field (`lead-scraper-filters.tsx:524`) and the uncapped leads-metadata industry join, which dominate the longest niches. Handled in ENG-10579.
* Filter-value cleanup (industries / titles / locations / sizes / keywords); provenance is not stored. No DB schema or migration changes.

## Acceptance criteria

* On the org's FIRST campaign, the niche field is pre-filled (editable) with the latest onboarding niche.
* On every SUBSEQUENT campaign, the niche field starts empty (no onboarding assumption).
* The onboarding niche is read only to pre-fill the first campaign's editable field; it is never written into a campaign's stored targeting behind the scenes, and `resolveSpawnNiche` (agent/backend) ignores onboarding entirely (explicit per-campaign niche or leads-derived industry only).
* A niche longer than 120 characters cannot be persisted: create/update/duplicate write paths blank it.
* Agent start-new / duplicate: an explicitly cleared niche stays cleared; a non-short incoming or source niche is dropped rather than inherited; a genuine short niche is inherited.
* The campaign's-own-leads metadata derivation (industry/title/location) still works.
* No NEW input-length UI/validation is added.
* Cleanup script: dry-run by default; blanks only over-cap niches and reviewed exact-onboarding-matched niches (temporally guarded); all-orgs apply requires explicit confirmation; touches only the niche column.
* Existing niche, duplicate, and approval test suites pass.

## How to QA (non-developer)

1. Finish onboarding (pick a niche). Create your FIRST campaign: the niche field should be **pre-filled** with that onboarding niche, and you can edit it.
2. Create a SECOND campaign: the niche field should start **empty** (it does not assume your onboarding niche).
3. Type a normal short niche (e.g. "HVAC contractors") and save: it saves and displays cleanly.
4. Have the agent create a replacement campaign from an existing one: it carries the source's short niche if it has one, and never a messy or oversized niche.
5. Open the campaign dashboard: it loads normally with no errors.

relatedSnapshot.title: Cold email agent: niche is always a short label (stop AI-search description + metadata-join becoming the niche)
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

When someone creates a cold email campaign, the "niche" should read like a short audience label ("Healthcare recruiters", "B2B SaaS", "Name 2"). Before this change the system could store a whole paragraph, an AI-search prompt, a long comma-joined list of industries, or the literal "Custom filters" as the niche, and that junk then showed up in the approval modal, approval emails, generated copy, and exports. This makes every niche a short human label and stops the system ever creating the long ones again.

## Problem

A real niche is a short label, but the product created long ones through three mechanisms. #4868 (ENG-10505) fixed only the first.

1. Onboarding inheritance. Fixed in #4868.
2. A2, the uncapped leads-metadata industry join. With an empty campaign niche, a comma-joined list of up to ~400 sampled lead industries became the niche and flowed into the agent plan, approval modal, approval emails, START_NEW creation, and SuperSearch keywords.
3. A3 (dominant), the AI-search description persisted verbatim. The "Describe the niche" box had a 3-char minimum and no maximum, so the whole sentence was stored as the niche, and "Custom filters" was stored as a placeholder. Prod had ~583 niches over 60 chars and ~301 over 120, reading like "AI Search prompt: Find US-based...", "Name 3:...", even pasted chat.

## Solution (shipped)

Stop the system creating bad niches:

* Keystone (ENG-8349): the stored niche is the campaign's own label only. It never backfills the canonical bestIndustry. The copywriter's targetIndustry keeps its separate bestIndustry fallback, so copy quality is unaffected.
* A2: the leads-metadata / filter industry can no longer become the niche. Only a single short industry may seed it. A multi-industry set leaves the niche empty.
* The "Custom filters" placeholder is never persisted, and a legacy "Custom filters" row now reads as empty via the shared isPlaceholderNiche guard, so it is not re-shown, re-inferred from in the AI-search box, or re-saved.

Always collect a real short label (derive-and-confirm):

* A new niche-label dialog. Before a new campaign first provisions, the user confirms an editable, required short niche label, pre-filled from their typed niche or a single industry plus role.
* A gate runs before all four first-provisioning exits (lead scrape, AI sequences, finalize, simple targeting). An existing niche is not re-prompted, cancel aborts before any write, and add-leads / edit are exempt.
* Server backstop: first-provisioning with an empty niche is rejected, and a niche:'' update never blanks an already-confirmed niche.

Caps and sanitize everywhere:

* Niche label inputs and schemas are capped at 120 chars (minimum 2). The AI-search prompt is capped at 200.
* A transient sanitizer blanks junk or over-cap values on every display, email, scrape, keyword, export, and CRM-prompt surface. Empty niches render as "Unlabeled audience".

Cleanup:

* A one-time script (dry-run by default) blanks existing junk and over-cap niches, logging prior values as a recovery trail. Name 4 runs it after deploy.

## Scope

Niche only (A2 + A3). Not the approval-modal UX / CSV provenance (PR-M, ENG-10580), not onboarding inheritance (#4868).

## Acceptance criteria

* Creating a campaign via AI lead search with a long description yields a blank or short niche, never the whole sentence or "Custom filters".
* A campaign with leads but no niche never shows a comma-joined multi-industry niche in the modal, email, or scrape. Industries appear under Industry.
* Every niche input enforces the 120-char cap, the server rejects or caps an over-length niche, and no transient, display, or email path shows a long niche.
* An empty niche renders as "Unlabeled audience".

## QA

1. Create a campaign via AI lead search, manual filters, or CSV. Before it provisions you confirm a short, pre-filled, editable, required niche label and cannot proceed empty.
2. Run agent approval on a mixed-industry campaign. The Niche is not a comma list, the email has no paragraph niche, and industries still show under Industry.
3. Enter a niche over 120 chars in a campaign form. It is rejected with a friendly message.
4. A campaign with no niche shows "Unlabeled audience".
5. DRY_RUN=true bun apps/web/scripts/cleanup-junk-campaign-niche.ts lists candidates and writes nothing.

## Links

* PR: <url:github.com>
* Preview: <url:pr-4947-feature-eng-10579-cold-email-agent-niche-aiacquisition.vercel.app>

## Open follow-ups

* Name 4 to run the cleanup script (dry-run first, then apply) after deploy.
* codegen-registry.ts (auto-generated, used only for exporting workflows to standalone projects) should be regenerated for the workflow-update niche cap. Name 5 runtime uses the source step directly.

relatedSnapshot.description:
#### Customer Name

Name 6

#### Customer Email

<email>

#### Workspace name

Company One and Company Two

#### Screenshot

 <image> 

 <image> 

#### What are you trying to achieve?

Client Name 6 needs three platform functions working, all currently failing: 1. Purchase new inboxes and domains in the Company Eight workspace . 2. Add and scrape roughly 1,000 leads into one of his campaigns in the same workspace. 3. Send a dashboard access invite to his client at <email> for the Company Two dashboard.

#### What are you doing to achieve it?

1. Inboxes and domains purchase: In the Company Eight workspace, went to Marketing, then Cold Email Agent, then Email Accounts, then Add inboxes. Selected the <domain> and <domain> domains, configured the inbox names, and clicked through to complete the payment. Has retried this many times over the past two weeks, restarting from scratch each time. Screenshot attached.  2. Lead scraping: Opened one of his campaigns, set the ICP and niche targeting (based on his discussion with Name 7), and attempted to add roughly 1,000 leads and start the lead scrape for that campaign.  3. Invite: From the Company Two dashboard workspace, sent a client access invite to <email> so his client can log in and view the dashboard. Sent it five times, using the email that matches the client's AIA account.

#### What is happening instead?

1. Inboxes and domains: the order stalls at the payment step ("Your inbox order is waiting for payment") and never completes, then cancels itself. On retry it returns "Payment failed: You already have an order in progress. Please wait for it to complete," so a stuck in-progress order is blocking every new attempt. The card is valid and has not been charged. The help desk has confirmed this as a known issue being worked on, but it remains unresolved after several days. 2. Lead scraping: fails with "Failed to start lead scraping: Niche must be 120 characters or less." The niche label exceeds 120 characters and blocks the upload. 3. Invite: the invite email never reaches <email> after five attempts, nothing arrives in his inbox.

#### What is the expected outcome?

1. The stuck in-progress order is cleared on the backend so the payment completes and the inboxes and domains provision. 2. The lead scrape runs successfully, either by clarifying or lifting the 120-character niche limit, or confirming the client can proceed by shortening the niche label. 3. The dashboard invite is delivered to <email> so the client can access the Company Two dashboard.

relatedSnapshot.title: Adding leads to an existing campaign wipes the campaign's existing leads while still consuming credits
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Name 13 signal (daily triage 2026-07-29)

Name 13 cluster *Campaign leads vanish after new upload, credits consumed* — severity high, confidence 0.88, **2 customers this week**.

* **Name 11 (Company Four)**: 5,347 existing leads in a campaign disappeared when she added more leads to it.
* **Name 12**: hit the same data-loss pattern today.

In both cases the leads are gone and the credits were still charged, so the customer pays twice to rebuild the list.

Name 13 topic: <url>

## Why this is a new issue

Duplicate search found no open canonical for "adding leads wipes the existing lead set":

* ENG-10981 "Scraped leads disappear after processing — credits consumed, campaign stays empty" — Done (2026-06-29); different trigger (initial scrape, not a second upload into a populated campaign)
* ENG-8186 "Cold Email Agent lead count resets after import" — Done (2026-05-03)
* ENG-7942 "Campaign upload loses leads and skips to step 4" — Done
* ENG-4551 "Missing ~760 leads after CSV import" — Done
* ENG-7247 / ENG-7186 — deletion/duplicate-skip behaviour, not data loss on add

Distinct from the stuck-processing cluster on ENG-10762: here the leads were present and are afterwards gone.

## Suggested starting points

* The add-leads path into an existing campaign: whether the import replaces rather than appends the campaign lead set
* Credit deduction on the second import happening before/independently of the lead write, so credits are consumed even when the resulting lead set shrinks

* Name 14 key: `modem_daily_triage:v1/<uuid>/2026-07-29`
* Window: 2026-07-28 13:02 UTC → 2026-07-29 13:02 UTC

relatedSnapshot.title: Let campaign analytics proceed for existing campaigns without legacy niche onboarding
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Existing active campaigns can fail the campaign analytics decision job with `No niche form data found. Please complete the niche setup first.` when their workspace does not have an old `niche_researcher` onboarding submission. We still want users to complete the niche setup before creating campaigns, but existing/imported campaigns should not lose analytics-agent decisions just because historical onboarding data is missing.

## Problem

`Process Campaign Analytics` calls `canProceedWithCampaignDecision()` before creating the decision log. That method currently treats missing onboarding `nicheFormData` as fatal for every automatic decision run.

Prod evidence from read-only DB and Axiom:

* Exact error logged June 15-17, before ENG-10505 / PR #4868 merged.
* 5 campaigns across 4 orgs hit the exact error in Axiom.
* 22 active campaigns across 15 orgs are currently in the at-risk state: active campaign, no `niche_researcher` submission.
* No at-risk active campaigns were created in the last 90 days, so this is mainly legacy/imported campaign fallout.

## Solution

Keep the creation gate strict, but relax the analytics gate for existing campaigns:

* Preserve the normal campaign-creation requirement that users complete niche setup before creating campaigns.
* Update `canProceedWithCampaignDecision()` so missing onboarding niche data is not fatal when the existing campaign has usable targeting context from campaign-level data.
* Use campaign-level targeting as the source of truth for analytics decisions, for example campaign niche, industry, job title, company size, location, saved settings, scrape/lead-search targeting, or other existing campaign targeting already used by the campaign agent.
* If both onboarding niche data and usable campaign-level targeting are missing, skip/notify gracefully without creating noisy Sentry regressions.

## Acceptance criteria

* Existing active campaigns with usable campaign-level targeting can proceed through campaign analytics even if the workspace has no `niche_researcher` submission.
* Campaign creation still requires the intended setup/niche flow.
* Truly untargeted campaigns still surface a clear action for the user/admin.
* The fix has unit coverage for missing onboarding niche plus existing campaign targeting.
* QA documents the Sentry/Axiom reproduction path and the post-fix behavior.

## Non-goals

* Do not remove the normal onboarding/niche setup requirement for creating new campaigns.
* Do not backfill old onboarding submissions.
* Do not change prompt behavior beyond allowing the existing campaign analytics flow to run when campaign-level targeting exists.

relatedSnapshot.title: Derive campaign data from existing leads when importing campaigns

## Overview

When importing campaigns, derive campaign targeting data (industry, title, location, company size) from existing lead metadata instead of parsing from campaign configurations.

* Strict country/company size normalization (validated against `COMPANY_SIZES` and `COUNTRIES`)

relatedSnapshot.title: Customer report: first-name-only CSV import leaves combined first and last name in the campaign leads table
relatedSnapshot.description:
Intercom conversation: <url:app.intercom.com>

Contact: Name 16 (<email>) · workspace: Company Nine (owner)

Bounded context: Customer imported a CSV containing only first names into a cold email campaign, then reported that the campaign's Leads table still shows first and last name together in one "Name" column. She had earlier exported a campaign CSV and removed the last-name column, and the campaign was already launched.

Finding (Platform Limitation, not a defect):

* Every leads table (campaign Leads tab, manually uploaded leads, workspace leads) renders a single "Name" column defined as full name, else first name + last name joined. The help center documents this: "Name | First and last name combined". There is no first-name-only display.
* On import, a lead that already exists in the workspace keep its stored names for any field the uploaded row leaves blank, so a first-name-only file does not clear a last name that is already stored on the existing lead record. Verified in code (bulk campaign-lead persistence: resolvedFirstName/resolvedLastName fall back to the existing lead/pool row) and in production: the affected campaign's imported leads all correspond to workspace lead records created earlier, and no new lead records were created during the import, yet the imported leads all carry last names.
* Mapping and the CSV are not at fault: the first-name column maps correctly, the stored first-name field holds only the first name, and {{firstName}} personalisation renders the first name only.

Open human action: reply to the customer in Intercom explaining the combined Name column and that last names cannot be cleared by re-importing; to show only a first name on a lead, clear its Last name via Edit Lead (affects future sends only). Reopens if the customer's CSV column mapped to the name field is shown to contain full names.

Bounded summary for resume: one live Intercom conversation, product/feedback lane, no money ask.

relatedSnapshot.title: Import leads through one ingestion pipeline
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Let integrations upload their own campaign leads and per-person custom variables through the API and MCP, then use those variables in existing email sequences. Deliver the endpoint, MCP tool, documentation and tests in one PR.

## User experience

The caller reads a CSV, maps its columns to standard lead fields and customVariables, and submits JSON lead objects. A 5,000-lead list is sent in batches of up to 1,000, with smaller batches when personalized content reaches the request-size limit. Callers receive an operation to poll, import counts and row outcomes, and can read back saved custom values.

## What's included

* One workspace-scoped bulk lead-upload endpoint and matching MCP tool, using the existing manual-import behavior.
* Existing custom-variable storage, UI and sequence rendering, with sanitized API readback.
* REST examples, CSV conversion/batching example, and a complete MCP mapping-to-sequence guide in the same PR.
* Scope agreed on 16 September replaces the earlier server-side CSV upload/parser proposal: CSV mapping happens in the caller, following Company Five's bulk-upload pattern. No new variable-definition product or file-storage flow.

## How it should work

Preserve existing validation, duplicate protection, workspace capacity and provider checks. Reuse shared idempotency and operation polling; retries must not duplicate uploads. Do not charge lead-search credits or automatically enable paid verification. Drafts remain drafts; adding leads to an active campaign may enroll them in its current sequence and must be documented. Import must not implicitly reactivate completed campaigns.

## Who can do what

Use existing campaign write permissions and organization-owned credentials. Derive the actor from the credential, enforce workspace boundaries, and preserve client-write restrictions. Never accept a caller-supplied user identity.

## Done when

* API and MCP can import a 5,000-lead CSV-derived list in supported batches with per-person values and safe retries.
* Existing UI and sequence previews resolve each lead's custom placeholders correctly.
* Invalid rows, duplicates, limits, capacity, permissions and partial failures have tested, documented outcomes.
* Existing upload and approval behavior remains correct after any shared-service extraction.
* The docs-only cold-start example works against preview; current-head tests, automated reviews and browser QA pass before code-review handoff.

## Implementation context

relatedSnapshot.title: Campaign Export Leads finishes with no CSV because the export's lead query fails server-side
relatedSnapshot.description:
Intercom: <url:app.intercom.com>

## Bounded conversation context

The customer manages two workspaces under one account: "Name 18 Agency" and "Name 17's Workspace". While planning a workspace closeout he asked, as item 6 of six questions, about the campaign's Export Leads function: it "finishes processing but does not produce a download". After the assistant answered only the credit question he escalated, item 4 of four: "The campaign Leads-tab export reaches 'Exporting...' but produces no CSV after repeated attempts. What alternative export or support-assisted method is available for preserving the 1,785 campaign leads?" He asked for written instructions only, with no changes, transfers, cancellations, renewals, or exports performed.

## Testable claim

The campaign Export Leads action runs, shows the Exporting state, and then produces no CSV download because the export request fails server-side with a database query error; the customer cannot export the 1,785 leads of the campaign "Name 19 - Hospitality - Name 20" in the Company Six workspace, and the button shows no failure to them.

## Evidence

* Worked example: 2026-09-11T15:30:44Z, outreach campaign <uuid>, organization <uuid>, user <uuid>. The export procedure logged "Failed to export campaign leads to CSV" with the driver error "Failed query: select outreach_campaign_lead.* left join lead_scrape_lead ... where campaign_id = $1 and organization_id = $2 order by created_at desc limit $3", params 5b95e219..., 8c6e269a..., 1000. The underlying Postgres error is not surfaced, so the exact failing predicate is not visible in logs.
* The campaign has 1,785 live leads, provider_lead_id NULL on all of them and 0 of 1,785 pushed to Company Five or marked sent, so the export's lead payload is not the cause of a query failure and the lead-push issue is separate.
* Blast radius (2026-08-01 to 2026-09-30, unscope: 1,457 export attempts, 1,419 successes, 11 failures across 9 distinct organizations. Failures are not size-correlated: three occurred on campaigns with zero live leads (organizations ecc419c7 and 298482ef, campaign ids 17f1d521 and d73d520c), and the rest on campaigns of 2,347 to 6,352 leads.
* The same organization and user exported a different campaign (b5d49b12, 338 live leads) successfully on 2026-09-02, which is why this presents as intermittent rather than as a hard failure.

## Impact

A customer who is closing a workspace and wants to keep his lead data cannot export it through the product and gets no error, only a button that returns to rest. The same failure pattern recurs across unrelated organizations, so the same silent loss of a data-export path can hit any workspace.

## Found so far

The failure is in the paginated lead fetch used by the export path, not in CSV generation or the browser download (Papa.unparse and the blob download are reached only after the fetch succeeds). What is needed is the wrapped Postgres error text from a failing export, which the current logging does not retain.
